title: Starlane Systems Activation Liftoff - Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for activation and onboarding of Redwood inference for Starlane's internal platform: discussed VPC topology, network egress, KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, initial pilot SLAs and runbook. Agreed next steps: share runbook + staging access, schedule performance baseline run, security questionnaire answers.
action_items: Evan Park: Share onboarding runbook and staging access instructions (due 2026-03-26)
Ravi Nair: Prepare initial perf baseline checklist and sample payloads (due 2026-03-30)
Anil Kapoor / Starlane Security: Complete Redwood security questionnaire and list of compliance questions (due 2026-03-29)
Maya Greene: Schedule 1-week pilot cadence calls and invite dev leads (due 2026-03-25)
next_steps: Customer to provide VPC peering details and sample traffic profile
Plan baseline benchmark (token distribution, p99 latency targets)
Security team to confirm acceptable KMS/HSM pattern and audit log access
questions: Can we route inference traffic through our transit VPC without NAT?
Is redwood dedicated offering able to bring-your-own-KMS?
What are realistic p95/p99 latency expectations for 2k token contexts?
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-23 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Evan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Greene (Redwood CSM), Ravi Nair (Redwood SE), Eve Morales (Starlane Head of Platform), Marcus Li (Infra), Priya Singh (Data), Anil Kapoor (Security)

Summary: Quick intro, tech intake and security handshake. Focus on pilot scope, networking, keys, and runbook handoff. Several side notes on cost/perf tradeoffs and fallbacks.

[00:00] Evan Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Evan with Redwood, i'll do a quick agenda then turn to Maya and Ravi to talk runbook and the technical bits, sound good?
[00:12] Eve Morales: yep sounds good, thanks Evan. excited to get this going. we've got about 40 minutes, so we want to leave time for the security questions, Anil has a few items.
[00:22] Maya Greene: quick intros from our side — i'm Maya, your CSM, i'll own scheduling and success metrics; ravi is our solutions engineer who will pair on the pilot setup.
[00:30] Ravi Nair: hi all, brief nod — i'll be the hands-on SE. just to note, we try to get a baseline perf run with your typical payloads asap so we can tune batching/kv cache.
[00:40] Marcus Li: yeah, we can share synthetic traces and production-ish payloads, we have a daily burst pattern.
[00:48] Priya Singh: and some of the prompts are multi-turn, so kv cache behavior matters.

[01:05] Evan Park: great, agenda: 1) runbook + access 2) VPC/peering and KMS 3) pilot success metrics and timeline 4) next steps. anybody want to add?
[01:16] Anil Kapoor: security questionnaire and SOC2 artifact locations, i want to clarify audit log access.
[01:22] Maya Greene: noted, we'll share our compliance pack and where to find SOC2 reports.

[02:05] Ravi Nair: on the running side — for the pilot we recommend starting with a small dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicaed) — sorry, the transcriber hates that word — dedicated capacity — that gives consistent p99 numbers and easier isolation. we can also start hosted then flip if you want faster time-to-value.
[02:28] Eve Morales: is the dedicated path required for our use-case? some of our workloads are latency sensitive but others are batch. we'd prefer one endpoint if possible.
[02:38] Ravi Nair: totally, you can mix. we usually do routing policies: latency-first for certain routes, cost-first for background jobs. since you have mixed traffic we can show an initial routing policy and keep a fallback in place.

[04:10] Marcus Li: networking question — can we peer our transit VPC and avoid NAT egress? security prefers minimal egress.
[04:18] Ravi Nair: yes, VPC peering and private endpoints are supported, and you can restrict egress. small caveat: if you want redwood managed control plane but private data plane, we have patterns (we'll share diagrams).
[04:30] Anil Kapoor: and what about KMS? we can't have keys in a vendor account.
[04:38] Maya Greene: we support bring-your-own-KMS/HSM — you can keep keys in your KMS and we do envelope encryption. we'll put the integration notes in the runbook.

[06:00] Eve Morales: excellent. on compliance, how do we get audit logs for requests and model versions used?
[06:07] Evan Park: we can provide token-level tracing in the console, and export logs to your SIEM. there are hooks for per-request metadata, we also keep an immutable model version audit.
[06:20] Eve Morales: ok perfect, that's a must for us.

[07:55] Ravi Nair: for the pilot success criteria — what Starlane needs to see: 1) p99 latency < 350ms on short prompts, 2) acceptable quality delta vs current generator, 3) throughput of X rps for batch windows. does that align?
[08:10] Priya Singh: yes though the 350ms seems aggressive for longer contexts, maybe p95 < 300ms for short. we'll share our expected token distributions.
[08:20] Evan Park: fair, we'll plan to measure p50/p95/p99 and include quality evals using your test prompts.

[09:45] Marcus Li: traffic shaping — we want to ensure autoscaling won't cause sudden cost spikes during bursts. how are burst policies handled?
[09:54] Maya Greene: there are autoscaling policies with burst caps and reserved baseline capacity. for Dedicated you can set reserved units plus brief bursts; for Hosted we can set throttles. we'll include recommended settings in the runbook.

[11:10] Eve Morales: one practical: can we pin a model version for the pilot? we can't have silent model rollouts.
[11:18] Ravi Nair: yes — model pinning and pinned rollouts are supported; you'll get an explicit version string and we only change on your rollout trigger.

[13:02] Anil Kapoor: i have a question about retention — how long are raw request bodies stored? we need short retention for PCI-ish flows.
[13:10] Maya Greene: customer-controlled retention for logs and payloads — default retention is 90 days but we can set it lower and provide immediate purge APIs. documented in the privacy section.

[14:40] Evan Park: ok, runbook link: https://redwood.example.com/runbook/starlane (we'll also attach a PDF). it has the VPC diagrams, recommended configs, kerberos-ish note — sorry transcription — the integration steps, and the perf checklist.

[16:05] Priya Singh: quick note, our prompts include tool-calling style structured output, will Redwood's function-calling or structured output hooks map to our downstream parsers?
[16:18] Ravi Nair: yes, we support structured outputs and can stream encoded events. we'll work with your data team on the schema mapping.

[18:00] Marcus Li: talking about telemetry, is there per-token cost breakdowns we can get in our console?
[18:10] Maya Greene: yes cost attribution per token and per-route is in console + can be shipped to your cost-analytics. we'll show sample dashboards.

[20:12] Eve Morales: timeline: what's realistic for pilot start? we want to hit a week-long pilot next week if possible.
[20:22] Evan Park: timeline depends on peering — if you can provide VPC details and service account, we can provision staging endpoints in 3 business days. so next-week pilot is doable if we get the infra pieces today/tonight.

[22:40] Anil Kapoor: i'll need the security questionnaire and the stub of required artifacts. can you send the SOC2 link and the list of encryption modes?
[22:50] Maya Greene: yes, sending now — SOC2 and compliance pack will be in the runbook bundle.

[24:05] Priya Singh: small gotcha — some of our multi-turn flows use long contexts ~4k tokens. will there be any kernel-level changes or quantization that affect those?
[24:15] Ravi Nair: we support larger contexts; runtime picks kernels based on model and sequence length. for quantized variants there can be small quality deltas, we'll recommend a quant-profile after initial eval.

[26:00] Evan Park: ok time check, last 20 minutes we'll assign owners and confirm next steps.

[27:10] Ravi Nair: i'll run the perf baseline: sample payloads, p50/p95/p99, and mem/kv hit rates. propose due 2026-03-30.
[27:20] Marcus Li: we'll get those payloads and an initial scale profile.

[29:00] Anil Kapoor: security still: what about SSO and RBAC? we need SAML-based SSO and fine-grained RBAC.
[29:08] Maya Greene: we support SAML SSO and fine grained RBAC; CSM will share the mapping doc.

[32:10] Eve Morales: ok if we wrap up with a short recap?
[32:15] Evan Park: recap: 1) Redwood to send runbook + compliance pack (Evan/Maya) 2) Starlane to share VPC peering details + sample payloads (Marcus/Priya) 3) Security questionnaire to be completed (Anil) 4) SE baseline perf by 3/30 (Ravi).
[32:35] Priya Singh: sounds right.
[33:00] Anil Kapoor: i'll review the SOC2 and flag anything, might take 48 hours.

[34:10] Maya Greene: i'll set up the pilot cadence invites for next week and include the dev leads + ops.
[34:20] Eve Morales: thanks, appreciate the clarity.

[35:05] Ravi Nair: any other technical risks we should call out? perhaps model fallback semantics and live rollbacks — we do have automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is an issue.
[35:18] Marcus Li: that's good to know. how do we see when fallback occurred?
[35:22] Evan Park: it's logged in the console and we can stream events to your webhook.

[37:40] Priya Singh: small transcription note — earlier you said 'KV cache' as something to tune, can you clarify how persistent that cache is across requests?
[37:50] Ravi Nair: KV cache holds per-session keys while the session is hot; it's not persisted long-term unless you set a prefix caching policy. we'll recommend settings for multi-turn flows.

[40:02] Eve Morales: ok final check — are there any blockers to starting?
[40:10] Marcus Li: not from infra aside from sharing peering.
[40:15] Anil Kapoor: not from security, pending the questionnaire.

[41:00] Evan Park: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll send the runbook and schedule the bench run.
[41:08] Maya Greene: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invites.
[41:12] Eve Morales: thanks, talk soon.

(typical transcription noise: some words mis-heard, 'dedicaed' instead of 'dedicated', a few proper nouns spelled off; see attached runbook for exact config names)

End of transcript.
